A region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=6{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2}),$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi }{2}.$ The area of the region is

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=6{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2}),$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi }{2}$ is 

$$
A={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /2}6{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))={sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2}).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /2}6{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{(x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)|}_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /2} \\  & =3[(\frac{5\pi }{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{2}))-(\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))] \\  & =3[(\frac{5\pi }{2}-1)-(\frac{\pi }{2}-1)] \\  & =3(2\pi ) \\  & =6\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The area of the region bounded by the curve y=6sin2(x2), the x-axis and the lines x=π2 and x=5π2 is A=∫π/25π/26sin2(x2)dx.

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the sin2 term: cos⁡2θ=1−2sin2⁡θ. We can rearrange the above formula as 12(1−cos⁡2θ)=sin2⁡θ.

Letting θ=x2, we have 12(1−cos⁡(x))=sin2(x2).

We can now integrate as follows: A=∫π/25π/26sin2(x2)dx=6∫π/25π/212(1−cos⁡x)dx=3∫π/25π/2(1−cos⁡x)dx=3(x−sin⁡x)|π/25π/2=3[(5π2−sin⁡(5π2))−(π2−sin⁡(π2))]=3[(5π2−1)−(π2−1)]=3(2π)=6π.
